title: UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) Skilled Worker Visa Framework and Digital Status
source: UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI), Home Office
content:
The Skilled Worker visa allows qualifying individuals to come to or stay in the UK to do an eligible job with an approved employer licensed by the Home Office.

Applicants must have a confirmed Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS), meet the English language requirement (CEFR level B1 minimum), and be paid at least the general salary threshold (or the going rate for the occupation code, whichever is higher). Physical Biometric Residence Permits (BRPs) are being phased out in favour of digital eVisas accessible via the online 'View and Prove' UKVI service.

The visa is granted for up to five years before requiring extension. Skilled Worker visa holders can qualify for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR / permanent settlement) after five continuous years of qualifying lawful residence in the UK.

title: National Health Service (NHS) General Practitioner (GP) Registration and Healthcare Access
publisher: Department of Health and Social Care, United Kingdom Government
content:
Foreign nationals relocating to the United Kingdom on visas longer than six months pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) during their visa application, granting access to NHS healthcare on broadly the same basis as permanent UK residents.

Upon arriving at their UK residence, individuals should register with a local General Practitioner (GP) surgery. Anyone in England can register and consult with a GP for free, and proof of address, immigration status, or ID is not legally required to register, although presenting proof of identity facilitates processing.

Emergency medical treatment at NHS Accident and Emergency (A&E) departments and NHS 111 urgent advice lines are free at the point of care for everyone regardless of immigration or resident status.

title: Transport for London (TfL) Public Transport Network, Fares, and Payment Systems
content:
Transport for London (TfL) oversees the integrated transit network of Greater London, encompassing the London Underground (the Tube), London Overground, Elizabeth line, Docklands Light Railway (DLR), London Buses, and IFS Cloud Cable Car.

London's rail system is segmented into concentric fare Zones 1 through 9. Travel payments operate on a fully cashless basis. Passengers pay using contactless bank cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or reloadable Oyster cards.

TfL enforces automatic daily and weekly fare capping, ensuring passengers are never charged more than the equivalent Day Travelcard or weekly pass rate for travel across the same zones. London buses operate on a flat single fare with the 'Hopper fare' allowing unlimited bus and tram journeys within one hour of first tapping.

title: Greater London Authority (GLA) Residential Tenancies and Tenancy Deposit Protection
source: Greater London Authority / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities
content:
Residential rentals in London typically operate as Assured Shorthold Tenancies (ASTs). Under the Tenant Fees Act 2019, security deposits are legally capped at five weeks' rent for properties with an annual rent under £50,000.

Landlords and letting agents are legally required to place security deposits into a government-approved Tenancy Deposit Protection (TDP) scheme (Deposit Protection Service, MyDeposits, or Tenancy Deposit Scheme) within 30 days of receipt, providing the tenant with prescribed protection certificates.

Tenants in Greater London are also responsible for Council Tax levied by their local London Borough council, alongside utility bills (water, gas, electricity, broadband), unless bills are explicitly included in the tenancy agreement.
